_voiceModelNote: Relative to the app root. The model is 63 MB and never committed: run 'npm run fetch-voice' to download it and its .onnx.json sidecar into voices/. MATIC_VOICE_MODEL overrides this path for one machine without editing this file.
_pythonNote: `python` is not on PATH on this machine; `py -3` is (handover §4).
_enrollmentNote: D282/D285 (2026-09-12). The tenant's enrollment secret, PLAINTEXT, per install - Charles's decision, because there is no installer to deliver it any other way (plan v3 §8.1 said this is a decision, not a default). Mint one on the hub - node bin/devices.mjs create-secret devco --ttl-days 30, or the console's Agents page - paste it here, and this endpoint enrolls at startup: POST /v1/enroll once, then the credential the hub returns ONCE is kept in per-user userData (enrollment.json, beside profile.json) and presented as Authorization: Bearer on every request. THIS FILE IS COMMITTED: the secret here must stay EMPTY in the repository, and test/enrollment.test.mjs fails if it does not. Anyone who can read a filled-in copy of this file can enroll a device into the tenant; anyone who can read a user's userData IS that user's enrollment. MATIC_ENROLLMENT_TENANT / MATIC_ENROLLMENT_SECRET override for one run. With no secret the endpoint does not enroll, says so once in the log, and works as before on a loopback hub (credentials are optional there, D283); a LAN hub refuses it with a sentence.
_providerNote: Which provider fills the tier-1 slot: "cloud" (Anthropic, the default - the demo build's request is unchanged), "local" (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint below), or "hub" (POST /v1/turn on the B0 hub in server/, at hubUrl). MATIC_PROVIDER overrides for one run. Tier-0 runs first whichever is set (D46b). Added 2026-09-03.
_localModelNote: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint - Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, or the customer’s own. Setting enabled:true SWAPS the cloud provider for this one; it does not add a routing tier. MATIC_LOCAL_MODEL / MATIC_LOCAL_BASE_URL override, and setting MATIC_LOCAL_MODEL alone is enough to turn it on for one run.
_voiceTuningNote: D264. HOW en_US-amy-medium IS DELIVERED - not WHICH voice, which is voiceModelPath above. Chosen by Charles on 2026-09-11 from a blind-ish listen to eight candidates, and the settings are the ones he picked. lengthScale is Piper own knob (below 1 is faster; 0.65 takes Amy from 3.03 to 4.16 words per second of speech, against the ElevenLabs Hazel reference at 4.59). shelfDb/Hz/Q are a high-shelf biquad applied AFTER synthesis in scripts/piper_worker.py: -2.3 dB at 2500 Hz, Q 0.7, which lowers the measured spectral centroid from 1377 to 1273 Hz - Q 0.7 because that is what reproduces ffmpeg treble=g=-2.3:f=2500, the filter used to render the samples he actually listened to. SET enabled:false FOR PLAIN AMY (lengthScale 1.0, no filter); MATIC_VOICE_TUNING=off does the same for one run without editing this file. THE FILTER CANNOT DESYNC THE MOUTH: a biquad is sample-aligned, and length_scale was measured to scale Piper own alignments exactly (timeline sum equals audio duration at both 1.0 and 0.65), so the viseme timeline stays true. THIS IS NOT THE RECORDED-GREETING TOGGLE - that is enabled in client/assets/greetings/greetings.manifest.json and turns off the ElevenLabs boot line. Two different switches: this one changes how Piper speaks, that one changes whether Piper speaks the boot line at all.
_restartPolicyNote: EVERY NUMBER ABOVE IS UNVALIDATED. They are policy proposals from research/2026-09-11-endpoint-telemetry-spec.md §6, which says of itself that there is no verified source establishing 30 days - or any figure - as an evidence-based restart interval, and calls itself educated guessing until validated against real ticket outcomes. They are here, and not constants in src/agent/restart-signal.js, because a constant is a claim the code makes and a default is a starting point a tenant can move. What would validate them: scoring recommendations against whether the restart actually resolved the ticket. Until that exists, treat a changed number as a changed guess. Omitting a key falls back to DEFAULT_RESTART_POLICY; the weights are overridable the same way. See client/docs/RESTART-SIGNAL.md.
_diskPolicyNote: UNVALIDATED, like restartPolicy. The dual threshold is the spec's §3 proposal: flag only when free space is below BOTH lowFraction AND lowBytes. It exists because a naive percentage rule fires on healthy machines - measured twice, on the spec's machine and on this one, where C: and E: sit at 17.5% free with 160+ GB of headroom and a "below 20%" rule raises two false alarms. gettingFullBytes is OURS and not the spec's: it only chooses a WORD for the row and flags nothing. lowBytes is 25 GB, gettingFullBytes 50 GB, both in bytes. DISK IS NOT A RESTART SIGNAL and must not be added to the restart score - a full disk is exactly as full after a restart. See client/docs/RESTART-SIGNAL.md.
